card.intuition: AGENTS.md is a file in the environment that the harness loads into the context window at session start — the project's standing brief to the agent. It is one way to avoid repeating the same corrections across every fresh session.
card.analogy: A shared onboarding checklist that every new hire reads on day one, so you do not re-explain the build commands, conventions, and do-not-touch directories to each person individually.
card.time_complexity: O(tokens in file per turn): everything in AGENTS.md is loaded on every turn of every session, so a bloated file burns tokens continuously regardless of task.
card.space_complexity: O(full inline content): instructions accumulate and dilute the context window, so the file must stay short and declarative to conserve finite space.
when_to_use: For content the agent cannot derive from the code, like build and test commands and hidden conventions
For hard constraints such as never editing a generated client
When you have corrected the agent for the same thing twice — that correction is a candidate line
gotchas: A long AGENTS.md both costs tokens and dilutes itself — the more instructions in context, the less reliably the model follows any one of them
Do not use it for content that should be progressively disclosed; a style guide belongs behind a skill or context pointer
Corrections only matter if the file is actually kept up to date and pruned

steps.label: Write
steps.annotation: The developer records build commands, conventions, and hard constraints in the AGENTS.md file.

steps.label: Load
steps.annotation: The harness automatically loads the file into the context window when a session begins.

steps.label: Act
steps.annotation: The agent applies the standing rules so corrections do not need to be repeated each session.

steps.label: Prune
steps.annotation: Long or rarely-needed content is moved behind a skill or context pointer to stop token burn.

exercise.prompt: Write a function that reports the token cost of loading an AGENTS.md file as directives. It must return the number of lines that start with a '-' bullet.
hints: Directives are marked by a leading dash
Increment the running counter inside the branch that detects a directive
exercise.test_code:
md = '- run npm test prefixed\n- never edit generated\nbuild notes live in TODO\n- deploy via vercel'
assert count_directives(md) == 3
assert count_directives('no directives here') == 0
print('PASS')
